verses.original: וַיְהִ֗י אַחַר֙ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה מִצְרַ֖יִם מֶֽלֶךְ־ מַשְׁקֵ֥ה וְהָאֹפֶ֑ה חָֽטְא֛וּ לַאֲדֹנֵיהֶ֖ם לְמֶ֥לֶךְ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
verses.transliteration: way·hî ’a·ḥar had·də·ḇā·rîm hā·’êl·leh miṣ·ra·yim me·leḵ- maš·qêh wə·hā·’ō·p̄eh ḥā·ṭə·’ū la·’ă·ḏō·nê·hem lə·me·leḵ miṣ·rā·yim
verses.literal: - Some time later . . . . . . - the king’s cupbearer and baker offended their master the king of Egypt

verses.original: פַּרְעֹ֔ה וַיִּקְצֹ֣ף עַ֖ל שְׁנֵ֣י סָרִיסָ֑יו עַ֚ל שַׂ֣ר הַמַּשְׁקִ֔ים וְעַ֖ל שַׂ֥ר הָאוֹפִֽים׃
verses.transliteration: par·‘ōh way·yiq·ṣōp̄ ‘al šə·nê sā·rî·sāw ‘al śar ham·maš·qîm wə·‘al śar hā·’ō·w·p̄îm
verses.literal: Pharaoh was angry with his two officers . . . the chief cupbearer . . . and the chief baker

verses.original: וַיִּתֵּ֨ן אֹתָ֜ם בְּמִשְׁמַ֗ר בֵּ֛ית שַׂ֥ר הַטַבָּחִ֖ים בֵּ֣ית הַסֹּ֑הַר אֶל־ מְק֕וֹם אֲשֶׁ֥ר יוֹסֵ֖ף אָס֥וּר שָֽׁם׃
verses.transliteration: way·yit·tên ’ō·ṯām bə·miš·mar bêṯ śar ha·ṭab·bå̄·ḥīm bêṯ has·sō·har ’el- mə·qō·wm ’ă·šer yō·w·sêp̄ ’ā·sūr šām
verses.literal: and imprisoned them - - in the house of the captain of the guard the same prison . . . . . . . . . where Joseph was confined . . .

verses.original: שַׂ֣ר הַטַּבָּחִ֧ים אֶת־ וַ֠יִּפְקֹד אִתָּ֖ם יוֹסֵ֛ף וַיְשָׁ֣רֶת אֹתָ֑ם וַיִּהְי֥וּ בְּמִשְׁמָֽר׃ יָמִ֖ים
verses.transliteration: śar haṭ·ṭab·bā·ḥîm ’eṯ- way·yip̄·qōḏ ’it·tām yō·w·sêp̄ way·šā·reṯ ’ō·ṯām way·yih·yū bə·miš·mār yā·mîm
verses.literal: The captain of the guard - assigned them to Joseph and he became their personal attendant - After they had been in custody for some time

verses.original: שְׁנֵיהֶ֜ם אִ֤ישׁ מִצְרַ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְמֶ֣לֶךְ הַמַּשְׁקֶ֣ה וְהָאֹפֶ֗ה אֲשֶׁר֙ אֲסוּרִ֖ים בְּבֵ֥ית הַסֹּֽהַר׃ וַיַּֽחַלְמוּ֩ חֲל֨וֹם חֲלֹמוֹ֙ אֶחָ֔ד אִ֖ישׁ בְּלַ֣יְלָה חֲלֹמ֑וֹ כְּפִתְר֣וֹן
verses.transliteration: šə·nê·hem ’îš miṣ·ra·yim ’ă·šer lə·me·leḵ ham·maš·qeh wə·hā·’ō·p̄eh ’ă·šer ’ă·sū·rîm bə·ḇêṯ has·sō·har way·ya·ḥal·mū ḥă·lō·wm ḥă·lō·mōw ’e·ḥāḏ ’îš bə·lay·lāh ḥă·lō·mōw kə·p̄iṯ·rō·wn
verses.literal: both of these men the Egyptian - king’s cupbearer and baker who were being held in the prison . . . had a dream . . . . . . on the same . . . night and each dream had its own meaning

verses.original: יוֹסֵ֖ף וַיָּבֹ֧א אֲלֵיהֶ֛ם בַּבֹּ֑קֶר וַיַּ֣רְא אֹתָ֔ם וְהִנָּ֖ם זֹעֲפִֽים׃
verses.transliteration: yō·w·sêp̄ way·yā·ḇō ’ă·lê·hem bab·bō·qer way·yar ’ō·ṯām wə·hin·nām zō·‘ă·p̄îm
verses.literal: When Joseph came to them in the morning he saw - - that they were distraught

verses.original: וַיִּשְׁאַ֞ל אֶת־ סְרִיסֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר בְמִשְׁמַ֛ר אִתּ֧וֹ אֲדֹנָ֖יו לֵאמֹ֑ר בֵּ֥ית מַדּ֛וּעַ פְּנֵיכֶ֥ם רָעִ֖ים הַיּֽוֹם׃
verses.transliteration: way·yiš·’al ’eṯ- sə·rî·sê p̄ar·‘ōh ’ă·šer ḇə·miš·mar ’it·tōw ’ă·ḏō·nāw lê·mōr bêṯ mad·dū·a‘ pə·nê·ḵem rā·‘îm hay·yō·wm
verses.literal: So he asked - the officials of Pharaoh who were in custody with him in his master’s . . . house Why are your faces so downcast today

verses.original: חֲל֣וֹם חָלַ֔מְנוּ וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֵלָ֔יו אֵ֣ין אֹת֑וֹ וּפֹתֵ֖ר יוֹסֵ֗ף וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֜ם הֲל֤וֹא פִּתְרֹנִ֔ים לֵֽאלֹהִים֙ סַפְּרוּ־ נָ֖א לִֽי׃
verses.transliteration: ḥă·lō·wm ḥā·lam·nū way·yō·mə·rū ’ê·lāw ’ên ’ō·ṯōw ū·p̄ō·ṯêr yō·w·sêp̄ way·yō·mer ’ă·lê·hem hă·lō·w piṯ·rō·nîm lê·lō·hîm sap·pə·rū- nā lî
verses.literal: We both had dreams . . . they replied . . . but there is no one - to interpret them Then Joseph said to them Don’t interpretations belong to God Tell me your dreams . . .

verses.original: שַֽׂר־ הַמַּשְׁקִ֛ים אֶת־ וַיְסַפֵּ֧ר לְיוֹסֵ֑ף חֲלֹמ֖וֹ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֔וֹ בַּחֲלוֹמִ֕י וְהִנֵּה־ גֶ֖פֶן לְפָנָֽי׃
verses.transliteration: śar- ham·maš·qîm ’eṯ- way·sap·pêr lə·yō·w·sêp̄ ḥă·lō·mōw way·yō·mer lōw ba·ḥă·lō·w·mî wə·hin·nêh- ḡe·p̄en lə·p̄ā·nāy
verses.literal: So the chief cupbearer - told Joseph his dream . . . In my dream there was a vine before me

verses.original: וּבַגֶּ֖פֶן שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה שָׂרִיגִ֑ם וְהִ֤יא כְפֹרַ֙חַת֙ נִצָּ֔הּ עָלְתָ֣ה אַשְׁכְּלֹתֶ֖יהָ הִבְשִׁ֥ילוּ עֲנָבִֽים׃
verses.transliteration: ū·ḇag·ge·p̄en šə·lō·šāh śā·rî·ḡim wə·hî ḵə·p̄ō·ra·ḥaṯ niṣ·ṣāh ‘ā·lə·ṯāh ’aš·kə·lō·ṯe·hā hiḇ·šî·lū ‘ă·nā·ḇîm
verses.literal: and on the vine were three branches As it budded its blossoms opened and its clusters ripened into grapes

verses.original: פַּרְעֹ֖ה וְכ֥וֹס בְּיָדִ֑י וָאֶקַּ֣ח אֶת־ הָֽעֲנָבִ֗ים וָֽאֶשְׂחַ֤ט אֹתָם֙ אֶל־ פַּרְעֹ֔ה כּ֣וֹס וָאֶתֵּ֥ן אֶת־ הַכּ֖וֹס עַל־ פַּרְעֹֽה׃ כַּ֥ף
verses.transliteration: par·‘ōh wə·ḵō·ws bə·yā·ḏî wā·’eq·qaḥ ’eṯ- hā·‘ă·nā·ḇîm wā·’eś·ḥaṭ ’ō·ṯām ’el- par·‘ōh kō·ws wā·’et·tên ’eṯ- hak·kō·ws ‘al- par·‘ōh kap̄
verses.literal: Pharaoh’s cup was in my hand and I took - the grapes squeezed them into [his] cup and placed - the cup in [his] hand

verses.original: יוֹסֵ֔ף וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ זֶ֖ה פִּתְרֹנ֑וֹ שְׁלֹ֙שֶׁת֙ הַשָּׂ֣רִגִ֔ים שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת יָמִ֖ים הֵֽם׃
verses.transliteration: yō·w·sêp̄ way·yō·mer lōw zeh piṯ·rō·nōw šə·lō·šeṯ haś·śā·ri·ḡîm šə·lō·šeṯ yā·mîm hêm
verses.literal: Joseph replied . . . This [is] the interpretation The three branches are three days . . .

verses.original: בְּע֣וֹד׀ שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֗ים פַרְעֹה֙ אֶת־ יִשָּׂ֤א רֹאשֶׁ֔ךָ וַהֲשִֽׁיבְךָ֖ עַל־ כַּנֶּ֑ךָ וְנָתַתָּ֤ פַּרְעֹה֙ כוֹס־ בְּיָד֔וֹ כַּמִּשְׁפָּט֙ הָֽרִאשׁ֔וֹן אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָיִ֖יתָ מַשְׁקֵֽהוּ׃
verses.transliteration: bə·‘ō·wḏ šə·lō·šeṯ yā·mîm p̄ar·‘ōh ’eṯ- yiś·śā rō·še·ḵā wa·hă·šî·ḇə·ḵā ‘al- kan·ne·ḵā wə·nā·ṯa·tā par·‘ōh ḵō·ws- bə·yā·ḏōw kam·miš·pāṭ hā·ri·šō·wn ’ă·šer hā·yî·ṯā maš·qê·hū
verses.literal: Within three days Pharaoh - will lift up your head and restore your position You will put Pharaoh’s cup in his hand just as you did when you were his cupbearer

verses.original: כִּ֧י אִם־ כַּאֲשֶׁר֙ יִ֣יטַב לָ֔ךְ נָּ֥א זְכַרְתַּ֣נִי אִתְּךָ֗ וְעָשִֽׂיתָ־ עִמָּדִ֖י חָ֑סֶד וְהִזְכַּרְתַּ֙נִי֙ אֶל־ פַּרְעֹ֔ה וְהוֹצֵאתַ֖נִי מִן־ הַזֶּֽה׃ הַבַּ֥יִת
verses.transliteration: kî ’im- ka·’ă·šer yî·ṭaḇ lāḵ nā zə·ḵar·ta·nî ’it·tə·ḵā wə·‘ā·śî·ṯā- ‘im·mā·ḏî ḥā·seḏ wə·hiz·kar·ta·nî ’el- par·‘ōh wə·hō·w·ṣê·ṯa·nî min- haz·zeh hab·ba·yiṯ
verses.literal: But . . . when it goes well for you please remember me and show me kindness by mentioning me to Pharaoh that he might bring me out of this prison

verses.original: כִּֽי־ גֻנֹּ֣ב גֻּנַּ֔בְתִּי מֵאֶ֖רֶץ הָעִבְרִ֑ים וְגַם־ פֹּה֙ עָשִׂ֣יתִֽי לֹא־ מְא֔וּמָה כִּֽי־ שָׂמ֥וּ אֹתִ֖י בַּבּֽוֹר׃
verses.transliteration: kî- ḡun·nōḇ gun·naḇ·tî mê·’e·reṣ hā·‘iḇ·rîm wə·ḡam- pōh ‘ā·śî·ṯî lō- mə·’ū·māh kî- śā·mū ’ō·ṯî bab·bō·wr
verses.literal: For I was kidnapped . . . from the land of the Hebrews and even here I have done nothing . . . for which they should have put me in this dungeon

verses.original: שַׂר־ הָאֹפִ֖ים וַיַּ֥רְא כִּ֣י פָּתָ֑ר ט֣וֹב וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־ יוֹסֵ֔ף אֲנִי֙ אַף־ בַּחֲלוֹמִ֔י וְהִנֵּ֗ה שְׁלֹשָׁ֛ה סַלֵּ֥י חֹרִ֖י עַל־ רֹאשִֽׁי׃
verses.transliteration: śar- hā·’ō·p̄îm way·yar kî pā·ṯār ṭō·wḇ way·yō·mer ’el- yō·w·sêp̄ ’ă·nî ’ap̄- ba·ḥă·lō·w·mî wə·hin·nêh šə·lō·šāh sal·lê ḥō·rî ‘al- rō·šî
verses.literal: When the chief baker saw that the interpretation was favorable he said to Joseph I too had a dream There were three baskets of white bread on my head

verses.original: הָֽעֶלְי֔וֹן וּבַסַּ֣ל מִכֹּ֛ל אֹפֶ֑ה מַאֲכַ֥ל פַּרְעֹ֖ה מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה וְהָע֗וֹף אֹכֵ֥ל אֹתָ֛ם מִן־ הַסַּ֖ל מֵעַ֥ל רֹאשִֽׁי׃
verses.transliteration: hā·‘el·yō·wn ū·ḇas·sal mik·kōl ’ō·p̄eh ma·’ă·ḵal par·‘ōh ma·‘ă·śêh wə·hā·‘ō·wp̄ ’ō·ḵêl ’ō·ṯām min- has·sal mê·‘al rō·šî
verses.literal: In the top basket were all sorts of baked goods for Pharaoh . . . but the birds were eating them out of the basket on my head

verses.original: יוֹסֵף֙ וַיֹּ֔אמֶר וַיַּ֤עַן זֶ֖ה פִּתְרֹנ֑וֹ שְׁלֹ֙שֶׁת֙ הַסַּלִּ֔ים שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת יָמִ֖ים הֵֽם׃
verses.transliteration: yō·w·sêp̄ way·yō·mer way·ya·‘an zeh piṯ·rō·nōw šə·lō·šeṯ has·sal·lîm šə·lō·šeṯ yā·mîm hêm
verses.literal: Joseph . . . replied This is the interpretation The three baskets are three days . . .

verses.original: בְּע֣וֹד׀ שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֗ים פַרְעֹ֤ה אֶת־ יִשָּׂ֨א רֹֽאשְׁךָ֙ מֵֽעָלֶ֔יךָ וְתָלָ֥ה אוֹתְךָ֖ עַל־ עֵ֑ץ הָע֛וֹף אֶת־ וְאָכַ֥ל בְּשָׂרְךָ֖ מֵעָלֶֽיךָ׃
verses.transliteration: bə·‘ō·wḏ šə·lō·šeṯ yā·mîm p̄ar·‘ōh ’eṯ- yiś·śā rō·šə·ḵā mê·‘ā·le·ḵā wə·ṯā·lāh ’ō·wṯ·ḵā ‘al- ‘êṣ hā·‘ō·wp̄ ’eṯ- wə·’ā·ḵal bə·śā·rə·ḵā mê·‘ā·le·ḵā
verses.literal: Within three days Pharaoh - will lift off your head . . . and hang you on a tree Then the birds - will eat the flesh of your body

verses.original: וַיְהִ֣י׀ הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֗י בַּיּ֣וֹם פַּרְעֹ֔ה י֚וֹם הֻלֶּ֣דֶת אֶת־ וַיַּ֥עַשׂ מִשְׁתֶּ֖ה לְכָל־ עֲבָדָ֑יו בְּת֥וֹךְ עֲבָדָֽיו׃ וַיִּשָּׂ֞א אֶת־ רֹ֣אשׁ׀ שַׂ֣ר הַמַּשְׁקִ֗ים וְאֶת־ רֹ֛אשׁ שַׂ֥ר הָאֹפִ֖ים
verses.transliteration: way·hî haš·šə·lî·šî bay·yō·wm par·‘ōh yō·wm hul·le·ḏeṯ ’eṯ- way·ya·‘aś miš·teh lə·ḵāl ‘ă·ḇā·ḏāw bə·ṯō·wḵ ‘ă·ḇā·ḏāw way·yiś·śā ’eṯ- rōš śar ham·maš·qîm wə·’eṯ- rōš śar hā·’ō·p̄îm
verses.literal: - On the third day which was Pharaoh’s birthday . . . - he held a feast for all his officials and in [their presence] he lifted up - the heads of the chief cupbearer - - and the chief baker

verses.original: וַיָּ֛שֶׁב אֶת־ שַׂ֥ר הַמַּשְׁקִ֖ים עַל־ מַשְׁקֵ֑הוּ וַיִּתֵּ֥ן הַכּ֖וֹס עַל־ פַּרְעֹֽה׃ כַּ֥ף
verses.transliteration: way·yā·šeḇ ’eṯ- śar ham·maš·qîm ‘al- maš·qê·hū way·yit·tên hak·kō·ws ‘al- par·‘ōh kap̄
verses.literal: Pharaoh restored - the chief cupbearer to his position so that he once again placed the cup in Pharaoh’s hand

verses.original: וְאֵ֛ת תָּלָ֑ה שַׂ֥ר הָאֹפִ֖ים כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר יוֹסֵֽף׃ פָּתַ֛ר לָהֶ֖ם
verses.transliteration: wə·’êṯ tā·lāh śar hā·’ō·p̄îm ka·’ă·šer yō·w·sêp̄ pā·ṯar lā·hem
verses.literal: But Pharaoh hanged the chief baker just as Joseph had described to them {in his interpretation}

verses.original: שַֽׂר־ הַמַּשְׁקִ֛ים אֶת־ וְלֹֽא־ זָכַ֧ר יוֹסֵ֖ף וַיִּשְׁכָּחֵֽהוּ׃פ
verses.transliteration: śar- ham·maš·qîm ’eṯ- wə·lō- zā·ḵar yō·w·sêp̄ way·yiš·kā·ḥê·hū
verses.literal: The chief cupbearer - however, did not remember Joseph he forgot all about him
